items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit strengthen security across complex codebases
items.summary_1line: CodeRabbit uses GPT-6.1 Sol to investigate security risks across complex codebases. Its security agent helps developers review findings and proposed fixes.
items.editor_note: First OpenAI customer story, applying Sol to security risk investigation and fix review.

items.title: DevRev delivers autonomous self-service with GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary_1line: DevRev uses GPT-6.1 Sol to power Computer and Operator, balancing reasoning, speed, and cost for enterprise service.
items.editor_note: Extends Sol to customer-facing enterprise service agents, framed around reasoning, speed and cost.

editorial.tldr: GPT-6.1 Sol surfaced on Oct 15 as the new Codex CLI default, reported at 77% lower cost by a third-party site. OpenAI then began publishing customer case studies on it, starting with CodeRabbit's security agent on Oct 26.
editorial.whats_new: OpenAI's Nov 4 DevRev case study says GPT-6.1 Sol powers its Computer and Operator agents for enterprise self-service, citing the reasoning, speed and cost balance.
editorial.why_it_matters: Sol is moving from a coding-tool default into production agents for security review and customer service, so its cost and latency now matter beyond Codex.
editorial.take_for_builders: Rerun your own agent evals on Sol and compare cost per task before switching defaults; the 77% figure comes from a third-party site, not OpenAI.

status.detail: Evidence so far is vendor case studies plus one unverified third-party cost claim; no independent benchmark is in the thread.

open_questions: Does OpenAI or an independent party confirm the 77% cost reduction in Codex CLI?
